author: 60 comments
text: 13h At Ramp, our price per million tokens is down about 80% this year. We got there while using a lot more AI. Every CEO I talk to wants the same result and asks the same questions about their AI spend: Which teams, departments and cost centers are spending what? What did we actually build? Was it worth it? It’s a hair on fire problem for most. Every other dollar a company spends has rigorous accounting behind it. AI spend doesn’t. That’s a missing piece of financial infrastructure, and the need only grows as AI spend does. So we built it for ourselves first. Here’s what we did: 1. See everything: We run every request through Ramp Router. We set defaults by workload based on cost, latency, and quality, rather than letting each team pick on its own. 2. Tag by task: We tag usage by task, not just by team or model. Engineering tooling and extracting data from receipts for our customers are very different jobs, and they shouldn’t be measured the same way. 3. Test on real work: We benchmark models, reasoning levels, and service tiers against actual workloads. Sometimes the most expensive model unlocks something new. Often a cheaper one does the job just as well, and we’d rather put those savings toward harder problems. 4. Rerun the math: Prices and capabilities move too fast for a quarterly or annual review. Every major release is a reason to rerun the benchmarks, not to switch right away. That’s how our costs came down while usage went up. We built Ramp Router and AI Spend Manage

The 105 enterprise accounts show that first-party data is what makes personalization work at scale. For Shopify merchants, the same principle applies on the product side: guidance is only as good as the catalog attributes behind it. Like Reply Tony Graham 14h Congrats to the Klaviyo team. As a lean DTC brand on the platform, the most valuable work I've done in Klaviyo lately isn't a new campaign, it's list hygiene: segmenting never-engaged profiles and sending promos only to people who've opened or clicked.
